_meta.source: 9-agent principled re-evaluation under the four correctness principles

rulings.justification: Two separate quirks with opposite verdicts. (1) The dp subtraction (Accruals.py L90-99) is NOT a quirk at all: Sloan 1996 working-capital accruals are (dCA - dCash) - (dCL - dSTD - dTP) - Dep, scaled by average assets. The script implements the paper; the engine tree (p1_factor_specs.py L526) simply omits depreciation. This is an ENGINE defect, proven cell-exactly on IBM 1990-01/1990-06, explaining 2.98M of 3.18M divergent cells. The engine must add SUB(..., dp) — that part is match_reference. (2) The script's positional groupby(permno).shift(12) over gappy m_aCompustat rows is a DEFECT under P1/P4: when a firm has missing months, position 12-back lands more than 12 calendar months in the past (proven: permno 28388 1966-06 pairs with 1965-01, 17 months back), silently computing a 'year-over-year' change from stale data of an unintended horizon. Economically the signal is defined as the annual change; the calendar-based wide-grid LAG(...,12) is the correct semantics and correctly yields NaN when the t-12 observation does not exist. The 15,359 residual cells are oracle artifacts and are accepted as a known mask, not reproduced. demote_to_script is rejected: the corrected tree fully expresses the sound part of the logic.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: Accruals: engine = [ (dACT-dCHE) - (dLCT-dDLC-dTXP_fillna0) - dp ] / avg(at, at_l12), with all 12-month differences taken as calendar lags on the wide grid (NaN when the month-t-12 observation is missing). Reference script instead uses POSITION-based groupby(permno).shift(12) over gappy m_aCompustat rows, so across listing/coverage gaps its 'annual' change pairs month t with data more than 12 calendar months old (e.g. permno 28388 1966-06 differenced against 1965-01). The reference is wrong: Sloan 1996 defines a fiscal year-over-year change; comparing against arbitrarily stale observations is an unintended artifact of Stata-style row shifting. Correct definition: value(t) - value(t-12 calendar months), NaN if either side missing. Residual divergence vs oracle: ~15.4k cells where the oracle emits stale-lag values the engine correctly leaves NaN.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. All inputs (act, che, lct, dlc, txp, at, dp) come from m_aCompustat rows already stamped with the standard datadate+6-month availability lag; both sides only reach BACKWARD (script positional shift(12) reaches 12+ rows back, engine calendar LAG(12) reaches exactly 12 months back). dp is the current fiscal year's value on the same availability-stamped row. No future information on either side.

rulings.justification: The script (BrandInvest.py L63-112) explicitly computes the Belo-Lin-Vitorino steady-state seed BrandCapital = xad/(0.5+0.1) at the first non-missing-xad row, then runs the recursion 'for i in range(1, len(gvkey_data))' over ALL rows after zero-filling BrandCapital (L91). Whenever the first non-missing xad is not the gvkey's first row (the common case — proven on IBM, first xad at row position 34), the recursion overwrites the seed with 0.5*0 + xad = xad, i.e. the seed the script just computed is silently destroyed and replaced by an unintended zero-fill accumulation. This is precisely the P4 pathology (zero used where no value is defined) and contradicts both the paper's initialization and the script's own intent (why compute xad/0.6 at all if it is discarded?). The engine's seed-preserving recursion (_op_brand_invest_signal, starts at first_pos+1) is the economically intended computation. Effect decays as 0.5^k after the seed year, so divergence is concentrated in early firm-years (IBM 1996: 101086.40 vs 101122.62). Do NOT adopt the prior proposed fix of replicating the overwrite; keep the engine and register the deviation.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: BrandInvest: engine seeds BrandCapital at a firm's first non-missing-xad year as xad/(delta+g) = xad/0.6 (Belo, Lin & Vitorino 2014 steady-state initialization) and starts the accumulation recursion BC_t = 0.5*BC_{t-1} + xad_t from the following year, preserving the seed. Reference script computes the same seed but then runs the recursion unconditionally from each gvkey's second row over zero-initialized values, so for any firm whose first non-missing xad is not its very first Compustat row the seed is overwritten with plain xad (effective seed = xad, not 1.667*xad). The reference is wrong: it zero-fills brand capital in years where none is defined and destroys its own paper-mandated initialization. Correct definition: seed = first_xad/0.6 at the first non-missing xad fiscal year, recursion thereafter; mask years before first non-missing xad and years with missing xad; divide by at; BrandInvest = xad0 / lag1(BrandCapital/at). Divergence vs oracle decays at 0.5^k per year after each firm's seed year.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. The recursion at fiscal year t uses only xad from fiscal years <= t; BrandInvest(t) = xad0(t) / BrandCapital(t-1). Script keeps December fiscal-year-ends and expands 12 months FORWARD from time_avail_m (datadate+6-month lag), keeping the latest past datadate on overlaps — all backward-looking. Engine uses the same availability-stamped annual panel. Neither side uses future information.

rulings.justification: The dominant quirk — re-timing availability from the earnings ANNOUNCEMENT date rdq (Cash.py L67-91: month(rdq) + 0/1/2, keep newest rdq per gvkey-month) — is DEFENSIBLE METHODOLOGY and in fact a more accurate point-in-time model than the engine's standard datadate+3-month stamp: once a quarter is announced its cheq/atq is genuinely public. The engine's ~2-month lag (proven on IBM rdq 2000-01-19) is not wrong under P3 (it is strictly more conservative), but it is not the reference definition and explains 1.08M divergent cells, so the engine should adopt rdq timing via a new RDQ_TIMED loader/op plus SMT-universe masking and atq>0. The values themselves match exactly, confirming a pure timing difference. However, the script's dedup (L46-59: dup=0 for singleton gvkey-rdq groups, keep dup==1) is a DEFECT: gvkey-rdq groups with exactly one row are silently DROPPED — an unintended data loss quirk of translating Stata's duplicates logic, not a research choice. The new loader should dedup gvkey-rdq keeping the first valid-atq row and RETAIN singletons, with the difference registered. demote_to_script is rejected: the logic is sound and expressible once the rdq-timed loader op exists.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: Cash: engine adopts the reference's announcement-date timing (quarter available from month(rdq), carried +0/+1/+2 months, newest rdq wins per gvkey-month, broadcast to permnos via the SignalMasterTable gvkey link, atq>0 required) — the script is RIGHT on timing and the engine's former datadate+3-month stamp was replaced. Deviation: the reference's Stata-style dedup tags singleton gvkey-rdq groups dup=0 and then keeps only dup==1, silently discarding every quarter whose gvkey-rdq appears exactly once in the panel — an unintended translation artifact, not a filter with economic meaning. Correct definition: one row per gvkey-rdq (first row with non-missing atq), singletons retained. Cells present in engine but absent in oracle due to retained singleton quarters are expected and correct.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean, with the timing traced explicitly: script stamps availability at the month of rdq — the quarter's cheq/atq is public as of the announcement date inside that month, and OSAP forms portfolios at the END of time_avail_m for next-month returns, so no future information is used; the +1/+2-month expansion only carries OLD data forward. Engine (current) uses datadate+3 months — strictly more conservative, also clean. Adopting rdq timing does not introduce look-ahead; rows with missing rdq are dropped rather than guessed.

rulings.justification: Every script 'quirk' here is a deliberate, documented research choice from Scherbina 2008 / the OSAP notes, and the ENGINE is simply computing a different variable. (1) The signal is a BINARY decline indicator vs 3 months ago (ChNAnalyst.py L74-82): 1 iff numest < numest_l3, 0 iff numest >= numest_l3 — the engine's numest/LAG(numest,1)-1 (p1_factor_specs.py L632) is a continuous 1-month percent change, an outright engine formula error (oracle uniques are exactly {0,1}). The apparent asymmetric NaN handling is cosmetic: NaN comparisons are False, so the indicator is defined only when the required operands are non-missing. (2) fpi=='1' restriction (L33) selects annual-horizon forecasts — a definitional universe filter; the engine's all-fpi pivot with aggfunc='last' mixes forecast horizons and is wrong. (3) The 1987-07..09 exclusion (L85-88) is a documented IBES data-quality window (OP Table 2). (4) The bottom-2-size-quintile filter (L92-102) is the paper's stated domain (signal only works in small firms) — a deliberate universe restriction, exactly the kind of filter the task definition classes as defensible. All four must be matched: fpi=='1' load filter, LT-indicator op with calendar 3-month lag, date-range exclusion, max_quintile=2 size filter on monthly mve_c. demote_to_script rejected — every piece is expressible with the ops enumerated in the prior proposed fix.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. numest comes from IBES summary statistics whose time_avail_m derives from statpers (the IBES publication date) — available in-month; the comparison reaches BACKWARD 3 calendar months (stata_multi_lag is calendar-based); mve_c used for the size quintile is the CURRENT month's market cap from SignalMasterTable, known at formation; the 1987 exclusion is a fixed historical mask. The engine's (wrong) formula also only used a backward 1-month lag. Neither side uses future information.

rulings.justification: (1) Denominator: the script (ChTax.py L33-50, L83) deliberately loads ANNUAL at from m_aCompustat and scales (txtq - l12_txtq) by l12_at — a deliberate design (it loads a second dataset solely for this), consistent with the OSAP documentation of Thomas & Zhang 2011, and empirically better-behaved: annual at has coverage in early/sparse-quarterly years where atq is missing (6/6 sampled missing-in-engine cells recovered, 200k cells). The engine's LAG(q_at,12) (p1_factor_specs.py L557) is an engine transcription error, proven cell-exactly on IBM 2000-01. Match the reference: DIV(DELTA(q_txt,12), LAG(annual at,12)) with the natural inner-join universe via NaN propagation. The script's lag construction is already calendar-based (merge on time_avail_m minus 12 months, L62-74), so no positional-shift issue here. (2) The unguarded division (L83) leaving +/-inf in the saved output (34 oracle cells with l12_at==0) is a DEFECT: a firm-month with zero lagged assets has no defined scaled tax change, and emitting inf violates P4. Engine maps zero-denominator results to NaN and registers the deviation.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: ChTax: engine = (txtq - txtq_l12cal) / at_l12cal with annual total assets 'at' from m_aCompustat as the denominator (matching the reference and recovering ~200k early-sample cells the quarterly-atq denominator would kill), lags calendar-based. Deviation: the reference leaves the division unguarded and its save step keeps +/-inf for the ~34 firm-months where 12-month-lagged annual at == 0; the engine yields NaN there. The reference is wrong: a tax change scaled by zero assets is undefined, and propagating inf into a cross-sectional signal is an unintended artifact, not methodology. Correct definition: NaN whenever the lagged-assets denominator is 0 or missing.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. txtq rows carry m_QCompustat's standard availability stamp; annual at rows carry m_aCompustat's datadate+6-month stamp; both are then lagged 12 calendar months BACKWARD (script via merge on time_avail_m - 12 months, engine via calendar LAG). The inner join pairs contemporaneously-available annual and quarterly rows only. No future information on either side.

rulings.justification: (1) The within-analyst-month aggregation: the script's own comment (ChangeInRecommendation.py L30) states the intent is 'the last non-missing recommendation for each analyst-firm-month', but L31-35 calls groupby(...).last() WITHOUT sorting by announcement date, so 'last' is raw parquet file order — proven on HAL 1999-03 where the oracle picks the chronologically EARLIER rec (anndats 03-09, ireccd 3.0) over the later one (03-30, ireccd 2.0). File-order dependence is a DEFECT: it is nondeterministic w.r.t. storage layout and contradicts the script's stated intent. The engine's sort-by-anndats-then-last is the correct implementation of the script's own definition; keep it (only 55 cells diverge). (2) The universe: the script's inner join to SignalMasterTable on tickerIBES+time_avail_m (L53-59) is DEFENSIBLE METHODOLOGY — it restricts to the standard OSAP point-in-time permno universe with SMT's own monthly ticker-permno mapping. The engine's broadcast via IBESCRSPLinkingTable produces 60,546 permno-months outside the SMT universe (and a static link table can attach a ticker's recs to a permno outside the link's validity period). The engine must switch to the SMT tickerIBES-permno mapping / mask to the SMT universe. demote_to_script rejected: both fixes are straightforward in the custom op.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: ChangeInRecommendation: engine takes each analyst's chronologically last recommendation in the month (sort by anndats before groupby.last), averages across analysts, computes opscore = 6 - mean and its 1-month change, then restricts to the SignalMasterTable permno-month universe via SMT's tickerIBES mapping. Deviation: the reference's groupby(...).last() is applied to UNSORTED data, so the analyst's 'last' rec within a month is whichever row happens to appear last in the parquet file — on multi-rec analyst-months this can select a chronologically earlier recommendation (proven: HAL 1999-03). The reference is wrong by its own stated definition ('last non-missing recommendation'); file order is not a temporal ordering. Correct definition: the recommendation with the latest anndats per analyst-firm-month. Affects ~55 cells (max abs diff 2 on the opscore-change scale).
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean on timing: both sides aggregate recommendations announced (anndats) within calendar month t and difference against month t-1's aggregate; everything is known by the end of month t, when OSAP forms portfolios. One mapping caveat resolved by this ruling: the engine's static IBESCRSPLinkingTable broadcast could attach a ticker's recommendations to a permno outside the link's validity window (a stale/incorrect-entity mapping, not future data); switching to SignalMasterTable's monthly point-in-time tickerIBES-permno mapping removes it. No future information enters on either side.

rulings.justification: The script's core formula (L49, L77: log((dltt+dlc)_t/(dltt+dlc)_{t-60})) is the correct Lyandres-Sun-Zhang composite debt issuance — 5-year log growth of total debt including current liabilities — and is defensible. The engine tree is an outright defect under P2: it omits dlc entirely and subtracts a spurious 12-month log-growth leg that appears nowhere in the script or the source paper (verified against IBM 1995-01: oracle 0.714663 reproduces the script formula exactly; engine 0.411396 reproduces the wrong tree exactly). However, the script's L70-71 fallback — fillna with a POSITIONAL groupby.shift(60) when no exact calendar t-60 row exists — is a script defect: on a gapped panel, 60 positions back reaches strictly more than 60 calendar months back, so the '5-year' growth silently becomes an N-year growth of unstated N. That is exactly the 'lags reaching further back than the stated window across data gaps' defect class. Correct treatment: adopt the script's formula but with a strict calendar-only 60-month lag — LOG(DIV(ADD(dltt,dlc), LAG(ADD(dltt,dlc), 60))) — and deliberately NOT reproduce the positional fallback, accepting NaN (P4) on the ~244,731 cells the oracle fills with mismeasured windows.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: CompositeDebtIssuance: We compute log((dltt+dlc)_t/(dltt+dlc)_{t-60}) with a strict calendar 60-month lag. The OSAP script (CompositeDebtIssuance.py L70-71) falls back to a positional groupby.shift(60) when the exact calendar t-60 row is missing; on gapped Compustat panels this reaches back MORE than 60 calendar months, so the oracle emits '5-year debt growth' values actually measured over longer, unstated horizons (~244,731 cells). The correct definition is a fixed 60-calendar-month window; where the t-60 observation does not exist the value is undefined and we emit NaN (P4). All other oracle differences were engine defects (missing dlc, spurious 12-month leg) and have been fixed to match the reference formula.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Inputs are m_aCompustat dltt/dlc keyed by time_avail_m, which already embeds the datadate->availability lag upstream; the script uses only t and t-60-or-earlier values (the positional fallback reaches OLDER data, not future data), and both the defective and corrected engine trees use only LAG'd past values. No future information enters.

rulings.justification: Every script choice is a deliberate, reasonable research design: (1) universe = SignalMasterTable (common shares shrcd 10/11/12 on exchcd 1/2/3) — a standard filter; (2) dividend indicator from CRSP distributions cash dividends (cd2 2/3) collapsed by ex-date month; (3) fillna(0) on div occurs only on SMT listing rows, where 'paid no dividend this month' is a genuinely defined 0, consistent with P4; (4) asrol (utils/asrol.py) gap-fills each permno span and returns the filled frame, so all rolling sums AND subsequent shifts are calendar-aligned — the correct semantics for 'last quarter'/'18 months ago'. The engine op (_op_dividend_omission_flag) is the defect: it builds from unfiltered monthlyCRSP (1,041,130 out-of-universe cells) and applies purely positional rolling/shift on unfilled rows, so across data gaps its windows/lags span more calendar time than stated and its row sequence is offset from the SMT panel (verified permno 12076: one extra 2008-08 row shifts every window). Fix natively: mask/base the panel on SMT membership — build_universe_masks (p1_factor_engine.py L2737) already reproduces exactly this filter — and reindex each permno to a complete monthly calendar over its span before all rolling/shift calls (gap rows NaN divind, matching asrol's min_samples=1 NaN-skipping sums). The wide calendar grid is the engine's native mode, so this is fully expressible; no demotion.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. The dividend indicator is keyed to the ex-dividend month (exdt), known by the end of the signal month; all constructions are backward-looking rolling sums (3/6/12/18/24) and positive lags (1/3/6/12), plus a backward 2-month extension window. Neither implementation reaches forward; the engine's positional-window defect distorts window length backward, not forward.

rulings.justification: The script formula (DolVol.py L30-34: log(vol_{t-2} * |prc_{t-2}|)) is the correct Brennan-Chordia-Subrahmanyam signal — two-month-lagged log dollar volume — and is defensible; the lag is a deliberate microstructure choice. The engine tree is an outright defect under P2: rolling 2-month mean of contemporaneous |prc|*vol with no log and no lag matches neither the script nor the paper (verified on IBM 1990-01: each side reproduces its own formula exactly; 8/8 sampled months). The one script defect is NaN discipline: np.log(0) when lagged vol==0 yields -inf, and dropna (L38) does not remove -inf, so 10,079 sentinel -inf cells survive into the oracle. Under P4, log(0) is undefined — a cell should carry NaN, not an arithmetic-breaking sentinel. Treatment: fix the engine tree to LOG(LAG(MUL(vol, ABS(prc)), 2)), mask cells where the lagged product is not strictly positive to NaN, and register the -inf deviation. The 1,825 miss_cand cells (oracle values from lag-2 months outside the engine's old rolling window) are resolved automatically by the corrected lag-2 formula.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: DolVol: We compute log(vol_{t-2} * |prc_{t-2}|) per the reference, but where the lagged dollar volume is zero (lagged vol==0) the log is undefined and we emit NaN. The OSAP script (DolVol.py L34, L38) computes np.log(0) = -inf and its dropna does not filter -inf, leaving 10,079 -inf sentinel cells in the oracle. -inf is not a genuinely defined signal value (P4) and corrupts downstream arithmetic (ranks would be preserved, but any moment/regression use breaks); NaN is the correct representation of 'no defined dollar-volume signal'. All other differences were engine defects (missing log, missing 2-month lag, rolling-mean instead of point lag) and have been fixed to match the reference formula.
rulings.lookahead_check: Script: clean — uses only t-2 volume and price. Corrected engine tree: clean, identical timing. The DEFECTIVE engine tree used month-t and t-1 vol/prc; month-t closing data is available at the end of signal month t under the OSAP t->t+1 convention, so it was contemporaneous rather than strictly look-ahead, but it destroyed the deliberate 2-month lag; the fix restores the reference timing.

rulings.justification: Two quirks, one of each kind. (1) DEFENSIBLE: the inner join with SignalMasterTable (DownRecomm.py L59) restricts output to the CRSP common-stock universe — a standard, deliberate filter. The engine's IBESCRSPLinkingTable inner join emits 62,230 permno-months outside that universe (verified: 0 of 62,230 in SMT); the engine must mask to SMT membership (build_universe_masks provides exactly this filter natively). (2) DEFECT: the script's groupby(...)['ireccd'].last() at L31-35 takes the last row in FILE order without sorting by anndats, so the analyst's month-end recommendation is whatever row happens to come last in the parquet — verified DANB/81695 2002-05, where the script selects the May-20 rec over the May-31 rec because the file stores them out of order. This is file-order-dependent, non-reproducible behavior with no economic rationale; the intended quantity is each analyst's LATEST recommendation in the month. The engine's anndats-sort-then-last is the correct implementation. Treatment: mask to SMT (match the defensible filter), keep the anndats sort (deviate from the defect), and register the 14 residual cells where the oracle is provably chronologically wrong.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: DownRecomm: We take each analyst's chronologically last recommendation within the month (sort by anndats, then last) before averaging across analysts. The OSAP script (DownRecomm.py L31-35) applies .last() per analyst-month in raw FILE order without sorting by announcement date, so when the IBES file stores a month's records out of chronological order the script selects an OLDER recommendation as the month's stance (verified DANB/permno 81695 2002-05: script picks the 2002-05-20 rec over the 2002-05-31 rec). The correct definition is the latest recommendation as of month end; 14 oracle cells differ and are script sort-order artifacts. Engine output is additionally masked to SignalMasterTable membership to match the script's intended universe filter.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Recommendations are grouped into time_avail_m by the upstream IBES table shared by both implementations; the downgrade indicator compares the month-t analyst mean to the month-(t-1) mean, both known by the end of month t (anndats within the month). Sorting by anndats selects the latest rec WITHIN the same signal month, which is available at formation; it does not reach into future months.

rulings.justification: The script's definition is coherent Barry-Brown methodology: age = count of the firm's rows in the SignalMasterTable universe (L31 cumcount+1), i.e. months of CRSP coverage — a firm with a missing price but a live listing still ages, correctly; and the left-censoring exclusion masks 'original CRSP firms' whose row count equals a calendar month counter anchored at 1926-07 (L34-40). The 30.44-day rounding is a crude but monotone month counter, and the anchor choice (firms entering at the 1926-07 official start are censored, while the handful entering at the 1925-12 data start escape, e.g. IBM) is a knowable, documented quirk of the reference, not an economically perverse outcome worth deviating over. The engine op (_op_firm_age, L929-935) is a defect on both counts: it counts non-NaN prc months (drops IBM's 2 missing-price months, so ages drift, up to permno 37560's large offset) and computes crsp_time as grid POSITION from a 1925-12 grid start rather than calendar months since 1926-07 — which makes the original-firm mask fire on the wrong firms and deletes IBM's entire early unbroken run that the oracle correctly keeps. Fix natively: age = cumsum(SMT_presence).where(SMT_presence) using the strict mask from build_universe_masks (which reproduces SMT row presence), and crsp_time = round((index - 1926-07-01).days/30.44)+1 from the calendar index. Both are expressible on the wide grid; no demotion.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Age is a cumulative count of past-and-current universe presence; the exclusion mask compares that count to a deterministic calendar counter at the same month. Neither implementation touches any future-dated input; the engine's defects are cross-sectional/anchoring errors, not timing errors.

rulings.justification: The script's design is sound Nguyen-Swanson methodology: base panel = SignalMasterTable (common-stock universe) inner-merged with availability-lagged m_aCompustat; pooled 60-month rolling regression of log market equity on accounting ratios plus FF48 dummies over months (t-60, t]; Frontier = -(actual - fitted); ceq>0 filter; xad fillna(0) is the standard Compustat convention for unreported advertising. The engine op (_op_frontier_signal, L1720-1731) is a defect: it bases the panel on UNFILTERED monthlyCRSP, so at each month the pooled training set contains non-common securities (verified 1990-01: 137 ADRs/REITs/units with shrcd 14/18/21/30/31), which shifts the fitted hyperplane and corrupts the residual for EVERY stock — proven by replication: rerunning the identical logic on the SMT universe reproduces the oracle to 1e-8 (IBM -0.35796345 vs -0.35796344) while the engine gives -0.75912476. This is not a formula disagreement; it is a universe-contamination bug explaining 1,218,262/1,221,162 diffs plus 92,222 out-of-universe extra rows. The op is already script-shaped and loads raw parquets directly, and the engine can build/load SignalMasterTable.parquet (L584-589), so switching the base panel to SMT [permno, time_avail_m, mve_permco, sicCRSP] (or equivalently applying the shrcd/exchcd strict filter to monthlyCRSP) is trivially expressible; also align the minimal-training gate to the script's len(train)>=3. No demotion.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. The training mask is time_avail <= current AND time_avail > current-60: the regression at month t uses only cross-sections dated t-59..t, and the month-t cross-section it residualizes is available at formation (contemporaneous in-sample valuation residual — a design choice of the reference, not look-ahead). Compustat inputs enter via m_aCompustat time_avail_m, which embeds the accounting availability lag upstream in both implementations. No future-dated information enters either version.

rulings.justification: Two distinct quirks. (1) Zero-denominator handling: the script (GrSaleToGrInv.py L77-88, L97-109) maps avg/l12 denominators of exactly 0 to NaN before differencing, letting the 12m fallback substitute — this is correct and defensible (a growth rate off a zero base is undefined; +/-inf is not an economic value). The ENGINE is the defective side here: _op_growth_difference_fallback (p1_factor_engine.py L945-950) divides raw, so 0 denominators yield +/-inf which is notna and blocks the fallback coalesce (35,008 inf cells vs 0 in oracle). The engine must adopt the script's DIV0->NaN guard on both primary and fallback terms. (2) Lag semantics: the script's groupby.shift(12/24) is POSITIONAL over observed m_aCompustat rows, so across Compustat coverage gaps the 'l24' value silently reaches arbitrarily further back than 24 calendar months (proven: permno 18331 @1954-06 computes the primary formula from sale/invt observed >24 calendar months earlier). This is exactly the defect class defined in the mandate ('lags reaching further back than the stated window across data gaps'), and it also diverges from the OSAP Stata original, where tsset-based l12./l24. operators are calendar lags. The engine's calendar LAG on the continuous monthly grid (template index is a complete date_range, p1_factor_engine.py L671; _op_lag L704-710 shifts on it) is the correct definition. So: fix the engine's division guard to match the reference, keep calendar lags as a documented deviation (~0.4% of cells where the oracle used stale-beyond-window data).
rulings.deviation_register_entry: GrSaleToGrInv: (a) Engine adopts the script's 0-denominator guard — primary = DIV0(sale-avg,avg) - DIV0(invt-avg,avg), fallback = DIV0(sale-l12,l12) - DIV0(invt-l12,l12), DIV0 returning NaN when the denominator is exactly 0, coalesced primary-then-fallback (reference-correct; prior engine inf behavior was a defect, now fixed). (b) DELIBERATE DEVIATION on lag semantics: the Python reference uses positional shift(12/24) over observed Compustat rows, so across coverage gaps its '12/24-month' lags reach arbitrarily far back (e.g. permno 18331 @1954-06 uses data >24 calendar months old and the oracle reports the primary formula where only the fallback is defined). The reference is wrong: the definition (Abarbanell-Bushee growth vs the average of values 12 and 24 months prior; OSAP Stata l12./l24. calendar operators) requires calendar lags. Correct definition retained by the engine: LAG(x,12)/LAG(x,24) on the calendar monthly grid; if the calendar month has no observation the term is NaN and the 12m fallback (itself calendar) applies. ~0.4% of oracle cells differ; those oracle values use stale data and are documented as reference defects, not engine errors.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. Both sides consume m_aCompustat keyed on time_avail_m = datadate + 6 months (CompustatAnnual.py L212-215), so accounting data is availability-lagged. Script positional lags and engine calendar lags both reach strictly backward (the script's gap quirk reaches FURTHER back — stale data, not future data); the fallback coalesce uses only same-month and lagged values. Neither implementation uses information unavailable at the signal month.

rulings.justification: Identical structure to GrSaleToGrInv with xsga in place of invt (GrSaleToGrOverhead.py L61-119 mirrors GrSaleToGrInv.py; same shared engine op _op_growth_difference_fallback L945-950). (1) The script's 0-denominator->NaN-then-fallback is correct methodology; the engine's unguarded division producing 6,472 inf cells that block the fallback is an engine defect — fix to match. (2) The script's positional shift(12/24) across Compustat gaps is a defect per the mandate's definition (proof cell permno 18331 @1954-06: oracle primary uses xsga=6.46/sale=290.4 from >24 calendar months back, where the calendar-correct answer is the 12m fallback). Engine keeps calendar LAG as the correct definition.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: GrSaleToGrOverhead: (a) Engine adopts the script's 0-denominator guard — primary = DIV0(sale-avg_sale,avg_sale) - DIV0(xsga-avg_xsga,avg_xsga), fallback = DIV0 over 12m lags, DIV0(.,0)=NaN, coalesced primary-then-fallback (reference-correct; prior engine inf leakage was a defect, now fixed). (b) DELIBERATE DEVIATION on lag semantics: the Python reference's positional shift(12/24) over observed rows reaches beyond the stated 12/24-month window across Compustat coverage gaps, contradicting both the economic definition and the OSAP Stata calendar l12./l24. operators. Correct definition retained by the engine: calendar LAG(12)/LAG(24) on the monthly grid, NaN when the calendar month is unobserved, calendar 12m fallback. Residual oracle diffs at gap cells (~0.4%) are documented reference defects.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. Same inputs and timing as GrSaleToGrInv: m_aCompustat time_avail_m = datadate + 6 months in both implementations; all lags (positional or calendar) point strictly backward; no future information enters either side.

rulings.justification: Four sub-behaviors. (1) Universe: the script right-merges m_aCompustat onto SignalMasterTable (Herf.py L36), so industry sales sums and Herfindahl shares run over the SMT universe (shrcd 10/11/12, exchcd 1/2/3 — SignalMasterTable.py L49). This is a deliberate, standard research universe filter: DEFENSIBLE, and the engine's current summation over all monthlyCRSP permnos with sale (_op_rolling_industry_herfindahl, L1079-1104) is the wrong universe (source of 1.58M small diffs). The engine must mask the metric panel and output support to SMT presence — expressible from monthlyCRSP shrcd/exchcd panels, so no demotion. (2) Broadcast: the script's transform('sum') assigns the industry-month Herf to every SMT firm in the industry, including firms whose own sale is NaN. DEFENSIBLE: industry concentration is an industry attribute; a firm need not have its own sale to bear its industry's Herfindahl. Engine's valid = values.notna() assignment condition (L1067) should be relaxed to match. (3) Empty industries: transform('sum') over an all-NaN group returns 0.0, so industry-months where NO member has sale data get tempHerf=0.0 ('perfect competition') fed into the 36m rolling mean. DEFECT: a P4 zero-fill where no value is genuinely defined — the Herfindahl of an industry with no observed sales is undefined, not zero. Engine emits NaN there (deviation documented). (4) Regulated-industry typo: Herf.py L86 excludes ["4812", " 4813"] — the leading space means SIC 4813 (telephone comm) is never excluded pre-1983 in the oracle, contradicting the stated Barclay-Smith 1995 rule and HerfAsset.py L85 which correctly uses "4813". DEFECT (typo); engine correctly excludes 4813 pre-1983.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: Herf: engine computes industry sales Herfindahl over the SignalMasterTable universe (shrcd in {10,11,12} and exchcd in {1,2,3}, listed that month) and broadcasts each industry-month value to every SMT member of the industry regardless of the firm's own sale being missing — both matching the reference. TWO DOCUMENTED DEVIATIONS where the reference is wrong: (a) the script's transform('sum') emits tempHerf = 0.0 for industry-months in which every member's sale is NaN (pandas sum of empty set = 0), injecting spurious zero-concentration observations into the 36-month rolling mean; correct definition: the industry Herfindahl is undefined (NaN) when no member has sale data, and the NaN is simply a skipped observation in the 36m mean (min 12 obs). (b) the script's regulated-industry exclusion list contains the typo " 4813" (leading space, Herf.py L86), so SIC 4813 firms are never excluded for years <=1982 in the oracle; the stated Barclay-Smith 1995 rule (and the sibling HerfAsset script) excludes 4812 AND 4813 pre-1983; the engine excludes both. Oracle cells present for SIC-4813 firm-months <=1982 are reference defects.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. sale comes from m_aCompustat (time_avail_m = datadate + 6 months) in both; sicCRSP and shrcd are contemporaneous point-in-time CRSP identifiers at the signal month; the 36-month rolling mean (asrol in script, pandas rolling in engine) is a trailing window ending at the current month. Cross-sectional sums use only same-month data. Neither side uses future information.

rulings.justification: The quirk is the inner merge of m_aCompustat with SignalMasterTable (HerfAsset.py L36), which restricts industry asset sums and output to the Compustat-AND-SMT intersection. That is a deliberate universe filter (common stock, major exchanges), consistent with Hou-Robinson replication practice: DEFENSIBLE. The divergence is an engine defect: _op_rolling_industry_herfindahl sums 'at' over all monthlyCRSP permnos, contaminating industry totals with non-SMT securities (1.31M small-shift cells, max_abs 0.978 in small industries; extra=22,807 non-SMT permno-months emitted). The fix — mask the metric panel and output support to SMT presence (shrcd in {10,11,12} & exchcd in {1,2,3} from monthlyCRSP panels) — is expressible in the wide engine (the op already loops per-month over cross-sections), so demotion is not justified. The at.notna() assignment domain already matches the inner-merge universe to within a handful of NaN-at Compustat rows; broadcasting to those rows too (as the script's transform does) completes exact matching. Unlike Herf there is no material empty-industry zero-fill exposure (inner merge plus the near-coincidence of at.notna() with the merge universe; miss_cand only 1,335), and HerfAsset's exclusion list has no typo, so no deviation from the reference is needed.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. 'at' from m_aCompustat carries the 6-month reporting lag (time_avail_m = datadate + 6 months); sicCRSP/shrcd are contemporaneous CRSP identifiers; the 36-month asrol / rolling mean is trailing with min 12 obs; industry sums are same-month cross-sections. Neither implementation reaches into future months.

rulings.justification: The script computes Investment = capx/revt with no guard (Investment.py L41), so revt == 0 with capx > 0 yields +/-inf; polars asrol rolling_mean propagates inf, so ANY 36-month window containing such a month gets tempMean = inf and the oracle emits exact 0.0 (finite/inf) for up to 35 subsequent months — proven on permno 92089 (revt=0 for 2008-06..2009-05, oracle = 0.000000 for 2010-05..2012-04, reproduced by rerunning the script). These zeros are artifacts of division by zero, not statements about investment intensity: a firm is assigned 'zero relative investment' for two-plus years solely because one historical month had zero revenue. Under P4 this is an unintended fill — capx/0 is not a defined ratio, and 0.0 is not a genuinely defined signal value. Same for degenerate all-zero windows: where the current ratio and the window mean are both 0, 0/0 is undefined, not +/-0.0. The correct definition is: ratio undefined (NaN) when revt == 0; the 36m historical mean is taken over defined ratios with min 24 defined observations; the signal is NaN wherever ratio or mean is undefined. The engine's current pandas implementation (_op_investment_to_sales_scaled, L850-854) coincides with this correct definition in output — pandas rolling silently excludes non-finite values, so the sampled cell becomes valid only at 24 finite ratios and equals the mean of finite ratios — but it reaches it via an undocumented pandas quirk; the op should make DIV0->NaN explicit (mask revt==0 before dividing) so the semantics are stated rather than accidental. The 2,894 beyond-tol and related missing-cell diffs versus the oracle at inf-poisoned/degenerate windows are reference defects (evidence tags this oracle_artifact). Not a demotion candidate: the script logic at these cells is precisely what is unsound.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: Investment: DELIBERATE DEVIATION. The reference computes capx/revt unguarded; revt==0 months produce +/-inf ratios which polars rolling_mean propagates, so the oracle's 36m historical mean becomes inf and the published signal is an exact 0.0 for every month whose trailing window contains a zero-revenue month (e.g. permno 92089, oracle 0.0 for 2010-05..2012-04), and degenerate windows can emit +/-0.0 where the math is 0/0. These are division-by-zero artifacts, not economic values. Correct definition used by the engine: ratio_t = capx_t/revt_t defined only when revt_t != 0 (else NaN); hist_mean_t = trailing 36-month mean of defined ratios requiring >=24 defined observations; Investment_t = ratio_t/hist_mean_t, NaN whenever ratio_t or hist_mean_t is undefined or hist_mean_t == 0; masked where revt_t < 10. Oracle cells that are 0.0 (or present) purely due to inf-poisoned or 0/0 windows are documented reference defects; the engine intentionally reports NaN or the finite-observation mean there.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. capx and revt come from m_aCompustat with time_avail_m = datadate + 6 months in both implementations; the 36-month rolling mean is a trailing window ending at the current month (asrol in script, pandas rolling in engine); the current ratio is divided by a mean of current-and-past values only; the revt >= 10 filter uses the contemporaneous value. No future information in either side.

rulings.justification: The script's logic is sound throughout: universe = SignalMasterTable inner-joined with monthlyCRSP (MomVol.py L36-40; SMT is shrcd 10/11/12 on exchcd 1/2/3), missing returns filled with 0 only on rows that exist in that universe (standard Stata-port treatment within a listing span), negative vol nulled, calendar-validated lags 1-5 for Mom6m via stata_multi_lag, trailing 6m mean volume (min 5), pd.qcut deciles/terciles with duplicates='drop' emulating fastxtile, tercile-3 gating, and a per-permno _n>=24 history gate (L110-121). Every divergence is an engine defect, not a script quirk: the spec wraps FILLNA(m_ret, 0) over the WHOLE grid (p1_factor_specs.py L757), so 31,868 dead/unlisted columns enter the 1990-01 cross-section as exact-zero momentum and poison the ranking (rank corr 0.75, 872,393 differing cells); _row_bucket's pct-rank+ceil (L938-942) is not qcut's value-breakpoint bucketing; and _per_permno_obs_num over pre-filled ret makes the >=24 gate vacuous. Under the new rules, demotion requires that the wide engine genuinely cannot express the script — it can: the engine already runs per-date cross-sectional loops (e.g. _rolling_industry_herf_one_month, _op_industry_adjusted_mean), an SMT universe mask is constructible from monthlyCRSP shrcd/exchcd panels plus row presence, in-span zero-fill of unfilled ret is expressible, a per-date pd.qcut(q=10/3, duplicates='drop') on the universe-restricted row is deterministic and implementable, and the positional obs gate can be computed from universe presence instead of filled ret. Therefore: fix the op to match the reference (pass UNFILLED ret + SMT mask; fill 0 in-span only; qcut-equivalent breakpoints restricted to the universe; obs_num from universe presence), rather than demote or deviate.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. Script: Mom6m uses returns from months t-5..t-1 (calendar-validated lags, strictly past); the 6-month mean volume is a trailing window ending at month t using volume known at month-end t; qcut breakpoints are computed within each month t cross-section from those quantities only; the _n>=24 gate uses only past presence. Engine: same trailing lag structure (_op_compound_return lags 1-5, vol.rolling(6) trailing). The engine's grid-wide zero-fill is a universe/fill-domain defect (P4), not a timing one — it introduces no future information. Neither implementation uses data unavailable at the signal month.

rulings.justification: The script (NetDebtPrice.py L68-70) computes the LEVEL of net debt (dltt+dlc+pstk+dvpa-tstkp-che) over contemporaneous mve_permco, exactly the Penman-Richardson-Tuna 2007 Table 4A definition. Its quirks are all deliberate research choices: the non-financial screen (L73), the require-nonmissing mask on {at, ib, csho, ceq, prcc_f} (L76-83, ensures a real annual report underlies the signal), and the exclusion of the bottom-2 BM quintiles via fastxtile on log(ceq/mve) (L86-93, the paper's constant-BM design). The engine tree is the defect: it computes a 12-month CHANGE of a truncated net-debt proxy (omitting pstk/dvpa/tstkp) divided by a 6-month-lagged mve — a different signal entirely, confirmed cell-exactly on IBM 1988-07 (engine 0.002915 = delta/lag6-mve; oracle -0.019712 = level formula), plus 1.2M extra cells from the absent masks. Ruling: rewrite the tree as the level formula on the SignalMasterTable universe with the missing-variable mask and the monthly fastxtile-semantics quintile filter (keep quintiles 3-5). The engine already performs per-date cross-sectional bucketing (_row_bucket in _op_piotroski_score), so a Stata-fastxtile-semantics variant is expressible; demotion is not justified.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Script: m_aCompustat time_avail_m already carries the annual-report availability lag from datadate; mve_permco is the SignalMasterTable market value as of the signal month (known at formation); the BM quintile is computed cross-sectionally within each month using only that month's data. Engine: LAG6(mve) and LAG12(net debt) reach only backward — stale, not future. Neither implementation uses future information; the engine's errors are formula/universe errors, not timing errors.

rulings.justification: Defensible in the script: the inner join of SignalMasterTable with m_QCompustat (L27-32) is a legitimate universe/data-domain choice, and the calendar-based lag construction via merges on time_avail_m minus 3..24 months (L38-51) is faithful Stata l#. semantics. The NaN-treated-as-positive streak logic (L57 comment) replicates the published OSAP/Stata definition, as does the streak>8 falloff to 0. Script defect (artifact): because chearn and its lags are built INSIDE the SMT-merged panel, months where the stock drops out of SMT delete quarterly observations that genuinely exist, and the NaN-as-positive rule then fabricates or truncates streaks (permno 84441 2006-03: real data shows streak 6, oracle says 0). Engine defect (must fix): _op_earnings_increase_streak L1160 initializes out=0.0 over the full month-by-permno grid and never masks — 42.8M spurious zeros where no ibq exists, a direct P4 violation. Ruling: mask the output to the ibq-availability grid intersected with the SignalMasterTable universe (this matches the reference's intended domain), but KEEP computing chearn and its lags from the full quarterly history rather than the merged panel — the engine's boundary tests use real data the oracle discards, so on the residual ~5,000 divergent cells the engine is provably more correct under P2.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: NumEarnIncrease: we output the streak only on months where quarterly ibq is available AND the stock is in the SignalMasterTable universe (fixing our previous grid-wide 0-fill), but we compute chearn = ibq - l12.ibq and its 3..24-month calendar lags from the FULL quarterly history, not from the SMT-merged panel. The reference script builds lags after the inner join with SignalMasterTable, so universe gaps destroy real quarterly observations and its NaN-as-positive rule then mis-states streak boundaries (~5,000 cells, e.g. permno 84441 2006-03: true streak 6 from raw chearn lags, script emits 0 because merged-panel lag rows are absent). Correct definition: streak boundaries are evaluated against the earnings changes that actually occurred, with the published NaN-as-positive convention applying only to genuinely missing quarterly data.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. m_QCompustat time_avail_m embeds the quarterly-report availability lag; all lags (l12.ibq for chearn, l3..l24 chearn for boundaries) are strictly backward-looking calendar merges in the script and backward shifts on the monthly grid in the engine. Computing lags from the full grid instead of the merged panel uses historical data only — data that was publicly available at the signal month even if the stock was temporarily outside the SMT universe. No future information in either implementation.

rulings.justification: The formula intent — 12-month change of ob / (0.5*(at + at_lag12)) with ob==0 set to NaN (L33-34) — is defensible and the engine tree reproduces it. The script defect is mechanical: L30 and L37 use POSITIONAL df.groupby('permno').shift(12), so across panel gaps the 'lag 12' reaches more than 12 calendar months back (permno 79901: 88 rows spanning 93 months; oracle -0.8915588 reproduces the positional shift exactly, engine -0.8471210 reproduces the calendar shift exactly). The original Stata code used xtset with l12., which is calendar-true — the Python port's positional shift is itself a deviation from the published definition, and it silently compares order backlog against data of the wrong vintage. The engine's calendar _op_lag (p1_factor_engine.py L704-709) is the correct implementation of the stated 12-month window; the 4,690 'missing-in-engine' cells are cells the oracle should never have produced (calendar lag genuinely unavailable). No engine change; document the oracle artifact.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: OrderBacklogChg: we use true calendar 12-month lags for both at_lag12 and OrderBacklog_lag12. The reference Python script uses positional groupby.shift(12), which at panel gaps reaches >12 calendar months back and produces values where the calendar lag is missing (4 value cells beyond tolerance + 4,690 coverage-only cells). The original Stata implementation (xtset + l12.) is calendar-true, so the Python oracle deviates from its own published definition; our engine matches the Stata/published definition. Correct definition: OrderBacklogChg_t = OB_t/avg(at_t, at_{t-12}) - OB_{t-12}/avg(at_{t-12}, at_{t-24}) with all lags at exact calendar offsets, NaN when any calendar lag is unobserved.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. m_aCompustat time_avail_m already embeds the annual availability lag; all references are lags (12 and implicitly 24 months back), never leads. The script's positional-shift defect pulls STALE data (older than 12 months), which is a mislabeled-vintage error, not look-ahead. The engine's calendar shift uses only past rows of the monthly grid.

rulings.justification: Defensible in the script: the SMT+m_aCompustat+monthlyCRSP inner-merge universe (L59-66), the fopt->oancf fallback (L76), the handle_stata_edges inequality semantics replicating Stata's missing=+inf convention (L100-114), the required-variable mask (L181-191), and the restriction to the top BM quintile with positive ceq (L194-201) — the last being Piotroski 2000's own design (F-score is defined for high-BM firms). Script defect (artifact): p9 computes l12_shrout with stata_multi_lag on the MERGED panel, so when the Compustat side lacks the lag-12 row, a shrout value that exists in CRSP becomes NaN -> +inf -> p9=1 — the firm gets credit for 'no share increase' precisely because merged data is missing (14,039 cells with diff = -1). Engine defects (must fix): (1) no SignalMasterTable universe mask -> 121,417 extra scored permnos; (2) _row_bucket rank-ceil quintile computed on that wrong, larger universe, shifting breakpoints (61,761 missing cells whose firms belong in quintile 5 on the correct universe). Ruling: mask to the SMT-merged universe first, then compute the BM quintile on that masked universe with pd.qcut-equivalent breakpoints — both are matching the reference's deliberate design. Deviate, documented, on p9: use the true CRSP shrout history for l12_shrout rather than replicating the merge-gap NaN->inf artifact. Do not demote: demotion would enshrine the p9 artifact, and the engine can express per-date quantile assignment (it already does per-date bucketing in this very operator).
rulings.deviation_register_entry: PS (Piotroski F-score): universe and BM-top-quintile restriction follow the reference (SMT+Compustat+CRSP inner universe; monthly quintiles of log(ceq/mve), ceq>0, qcut breakpoints; keep quintile 5 only). Documented deviation on component p9 (no share increase): we evaluate shrout_t <= shrout_{t-12} using the true CRSP shrout history at calendar lag 12. The reference computes l12_shrout inside the three-way merged panel, so a missing Compustat lag row nulls a shrout value that exists in CRSP, and its Stata missing=+inf convention then awards p9=1 — firms that actually issued shares get credit for not issuing (~14,000 cells, engine 1 point lower). Correct definition: p9 uses the actual share count 12 calendar months prior wherever CRSP observed it; the missing=+inf convention applies only when the lag-12 share count genuinely does not exist.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. All fundamentals come from m_aCompustat with the annual availability lag baked into time_avail_m; shrout is the CRSP month-end value of the (already availability-lagged) signal month; all comparisons use 12-month backward lags (fill_date_gaps + stata_multi_lag in the script is calendar-true; engine _op_lag is calendar-true); the BM quintile is computed within each month cross-sectionally. No leads anywhere in either implementation.

rulings.justification: Defensible in the script: aggregating to one recommendation per analyst-firm-month, taking the monthly cross-analyst mean, flagging a decrease vs the prior month's mean as an upgrade, requiring a non-missing lag (L50-52), and inner-joining to SignalMasterTable (L62) — including the fan-out to multiple permnos when SMT maps one IBES ticker to two securities (e.g. CIT1 1993-11 -> 23879 and 23887). Script defect: L31-35 takes groupby(...)['ireccd'].last() WITHOUT sorting by anndats, so 'the analyst's last recommendation of the month' is whatever row happens to come last in parquet file order — nondeterministic and economically unintended (MRBA 1999-05: chronological last is ireccd 3.0 on 5/27, file order returns the 5/25 rec). Engine defects (must fix): (1) no SMT universe mask — 62,230 extra cells, 1000/1000 sampled outside SMT; (2) _ibes_permno_month_map drop_duplicates keep='first' (L518) silently discards secondary permnos of a ticker-month, dropping 109 legitimate cells. Ruling: keep all (tickerIBES, permno) pairs and mask output to the SMT universe (matching the reference), and KEEP the anndats sort in _prepare_recommendation_monthly (L1471) — chronological ordering is the correct reading of 'last recommendation', and the 8 flip cells are an oracle artifact of arbitrary file order.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: UpRecomm: we select each analyst's last recommendation of the month by announcement date (anndats ascending, take last). The reference script calls groupby(...).last() on the raw parquet row order with no date sort, so its within-month 'last' depends on arbitrary file ordering and flips the signal where an analyst revised twice in a month (8 cells, e.g. MRBA 1999-05: anndats 5/25 ireccd 2.0 then 5/27 ireccd 3.0; file order keeps 2.0, chronology keeps 3.0). Correct definition: the analyst's month-end stance is the chronologically latest recommendation by anndats. Universe and multi-permno fan-out follow the reference (all SMT (tickerIBES, permno) pairs, output masked to SignalMasterTable).
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Recommendations enter at the month of their announcement (anndats within time_avail_m, known by month end under the OSAP availability convention shared by script and engine); the upgrade test compares the current month's mean against the 1-month-lagged mean — strictly backward. The anndats sort orders only within-month history already announced. No future information in either implementation.

rulings.justification: Defensible in the script: the fpi==1 filter, the 30-day fpedats validity flag with conditional fill-forward of meanest when the forecast period is unchanged (L29-51, standard IBES hygiene), building the panel on SignalMasterTable rows with SMT prc (L60-68), scaling the revision by the prior month's absolute price, and the strict 7-term skipna=False sum (L91) requiring a complete 6-month window. Script defect: L74-75 use POSITIONAL groupby('permno').shift(1) on the SMT panel, so across an SMT gap the '1-month lag' is months stale — permno 62519 at 1995-05 divides by a 12-month-old price of 4.00 (vs actual ~16.75), producing REV6=0.16025, a 50x distortion; the original Stata l. operator is calendar-true and would return missing. Engine defects (must fix): (1) base panel built from the deduped IBESCRSPLinkingTable + monthlyCRSP prc instead of SMT (L2315-2320) — 188,095 extra cells outside SMT, and keep='first' dedup (L518) drops secondary permnos (1,086 missing cells); (2) no SMT mask. Ruling: rebuild the base panel from SignalMasterTable (permno, tickerIBES, prc) with full multi-permno fan-out and mask output to SMT (matching the reference universe and price source), but use calendar-true 1-month and 1..6-month lags, NOT the oracle's row-positional shifts; document the 91 gap cells as an oracle artifact.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: REV6: base panel, price source, and universe follow the reference (SignalMasterTable rows and prc, all (tickerIBES, permno) pairs, output restricted to SMT), but all lags — meanest_lag1, prc_lag1, and the six tempRev lags — are true calendar-month lags, missing when the prior calendar month is unobserved. The reference Python script uses positional groupby.shift over SMT row order, so at listing gaps it treats a many-months-old estimate/price as the 1-month lag (permno 62519/BLK 1995-05: divides by a price from 1994-05, 12 months stale, REV6 0.16025 vs 0.0030 with true lags; 91 affected cells). The original Stata l. operator is calendar-true and would yield missing there, so the oracle deviates from its own published definition. Correct definition: tempRev_t = (meanest_t - meanest_{t-1})/|prc_{t-1}| at exact calendar offsets; REV6_t = sum of tempRev_{t-5..t} plus current per the 7-term window, NaN if any calendar term is missing.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. meanest is the IBES consensus with statpers inside the signal month (available under the shared OSAP time_avail_m convention); the fill-forward uses only the PRIOR row's estimate; the scaling price and all 6 revision lags are backward-looking. The script's positional-shift defect substitutes STALE data for the 1-month lag — a wrong-vintage error, not look-ahead. fpedats in the validity flag is a fixed attribute of the forecast (its period end date), not future market information. Neither implementation uses future data.

rulings.justification: Three distinct quirks. (1) SMT inner-merge (L73): a deliberate universe filter (shrcd/exchcd common-stock universe) — defensible methodology; the engine's 301,508 extras on the unfiltered m_aCompustat grid (only 1.07% of sampled extras in SMT) are an engine deviation and must be eliminated by masking to the SMT universe. (2) The capx patch (L105-106: capx := ppent - l12_ppent where capx missing and FirmAge>=24, with CRSP-start censoring L91-97): a deliberate imputation from Anderson & Garcia-Feijoo's design — defensible in intent, and it explains all 159,521 sampled misses; the engine should adopt it. (3) Positional shift(12/24) on the SMT-inner-merged, gapped panel (L110-112) plus FirmAge as row position (L86) on that same gapped panel: DEFECTS. The Stata original's l24.capx under tsset is calendar-based; the Python port silently converted it to positional, so when a permno drops out of the SMT universe and re-enters, the 'l24' lag reaches arbitrarily further back than 24 months (verified: permno 36767 1974-07 oracle=26.107 built from a capx across a gap vs engine's correct calendar t-24 value 1.2324). This is exactly the 'lags reaching further back than the stated window across data gaps' defect class and is not a research choice — it is a porting artifact. Engine treatment: keep calendar LAG semantics (correct), add the SMT universe mask, add the patch as COALESCE(capx, WHERE(firm_age>=24, SUB(ppent, LAG(ppent,12)))) with firm_age computed calendar-wise from first SMT appearance and censored at CRSP start, and map zero l24_capx denominators to NaN rather than inf. Demotion is rejected: the script's lag logic is unsound, so demoting would enshrine the defect (P2 forbids treating the fallible reference as ground truth).
rulings.deviation_register_entry: grcapx: We deviate from ZZ1_grcapx_grcapx1y_grcapx3y.py in three ways. (a) Lags are calendar-based: l24.capx means capx at time_avail_m minus 24 calendar months, NaN if that month is absent. The script uses positional groupby.shift(24) on the SMT-inner-merged panel, so across universe-exit gaps its 'l24' silently reaches >24 months back (e.g. permno 36767 1974-07); the Stata source (tsset + l24.) is calendar-based, so the Python script is unfaithful to its own reference. (b) FirmAge is months since first SMT appearance (calendar), censored where listing predates CRSP coverage start, not a row-position count on a gapped panel. (c) Zero l24 capx denominators yield NaN, never inf (script's save path can retain non-finite values). We DO adopt the script's deliberate choices: SMT universe mask and the missing-capx := ppent - l12_ppent patch for firms aged >= 24 months.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. All inputs are m_aCompustat columns keyed on time_avail_m (already availability-lagged from datadate); the patch uses ppent at t and t-12; FirmAge/tempcrsptime use only listing history up to t; all lags reach backward. The script's positional-lag defect fetches data that is too OLD (stale), not future data — a P2 correctness issue, not a P3 violation.

rulings.justification: Same script and same decomposition as grcapx: the formula itself is fine (L124 capx/(l12+l24+l36)*3 is algebraically identical to the tree's 3*capx/sum, confirmed by exact IBM match), the SMT inner-merge universe filter and the ppent-based capx patch are defensible methodology the engine must adopt (they explain the 266,209 extras at 1.2% SMT membership and all 200/200 sampled misses), and the positional shift(12/24/36) on the gapped SMT-merged panel is a porting DEFECT for the same reason as grcapx — Stata calendar lags were silently converted to positional lags that bridge universe-exit gaps. Additionally, both sides currently emit inf when the three-lag sum is zero (script retains 2,332 inf via save_predictor, engine 3,016): an economically meaningless non-finite output that is a defect wherever it occurs; correct definition maps zero denominator to NaN. Ruling: fix the engine tree (SMT mask + patch coalesce + calendar lags + zero-denominator -> NaN) and register the calendar-lag and NaN-denominator deviations. Demotion rejected on the same P2 grounds as grcapx — the script's lag semantics are provably wrong relative to its own Stata source.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: grcapx3y: Same register entry as grcapx items (a)-(c) — calendar lags at 12/24/36 months instead of the script's positional shifts on the gapped SMT panel; calendar FirmAge for the capx patch gate; and additionally the denominator (l12_capx + l24_capx + l36_capx) == 0 yields NaN, whereas both the script (2,332 cells) and the previous engine (3,016 cells) emitted inf. SMT universe mask and the ppent capx patch are adopted as the reference's deliberate methodology.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Identical input timing to grcapx (capx/ppent at t, t-12, t-24, t-36 on availability-lagged time_avail_m). Positional-lag gap-bridging pulls stale past data, never future data.

rulings.justification: Every script quirk here is a deliberate, economically sensible research design, and every discrepancy is an engine defect. (1) Industry from sicCRSP (SMT, string-truncated 2-digit, L47-48), not Compustat sic: a deliberate input choice (documented in the script header, consistent with Tuzel 2010 using CRSP classification); proven decisive at IBM 2000-06 (Compustat sic 7370 -> '73' vs sicCRSP -> '35'), and since it shifts every industry mean, 1,432,529 of 1,432,612 both-valued cells are off — the engine is computing a different factor. (2) SMT inner join (L40-44): deliberate universe filter; kills the 168,741 engine extras. (3) inf -> NaN scrub before the industry mean (L69): correct handling of division by zero — the engine's 1,710 retained infs poison industry means and are a defect on the engine side. (4) The >=5 gate counts non-null 'at' per (sic2D, month) BEFORE the at/ppegt row drops and before re exists (L51-52): a deliberate industry-size screen ('industry must have at least 5 asset-reporting firms') even though the effective n entering the mean can be smaller; a reasonable, if slightly loose, sample-selection rule — not a silent error. The engine's gate on non-null re count (p1_factor_engine.py L896-898) is a different rule and must change. All four fixes are expressible in the wide grid (sicCRSP input panel; SMT mask; inf-scrub in the ratio; industry_adjusted_mean gaining a count_basis input), so demotion is not warranted. No deviation from the reference is retained.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Inputs are balance-sheet items (ppenb, ppenls, fatb, fatl, ppegt, ppent, at) at time_avail_m (availability-lagged) and sicCRSP as of the same month from SMT; the industry mean is a contemporaneous same-month cross-section. Neither implementation reaches forward in time.

rulings.justification: Two quirks with opposite verdicts. (1) The zero-denominator guard (script L66-70: l12_at == 0 -> NaN): correct and deliberate — an asset base of zero makes growth undefined; the engine's 30 extra cells are all inf from plain division (e.g. permno 82716, at@t-12 = 0.0) and are an engine defect to fix via WHERE(EQ(LAG(at,12),0), NaN, ...) or a zero->NaN div mode. (2) The positional groupby.shift(12) (L63): a DEFECT — m_aCompustat has real gaps, and 400/400 sampled missing-in-engine cells are cases where the script's shift reached an observation more than 12 calendar months back, producing '12-month asset growth' computed over a longer, permno-varying horizon. That is the prompt's defect class verbatim (lag reaching beyond the stated window across gaps) and an oracle artifact, not methodology; the engine's calendar LAG(at,12), which returns NaN when t-12 is unobserved (P4: no value where none is defined), is the correct definition. The 15,556 oracle-only cells are therefore rejected rather than reproduced. With 0 beyond-tolerance cells on 3.2M both-valued observations, the remaining fix is small and fully tree-expressible, so demotion is unnecessary and would only re-import the defect.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: AssetGrowth: We deviate from AssetGrowth.py's lag construction. The script's groupby(permno).shift(12) is positional and, across gaps in m_aCompustat, silently computes 'annual' growth from an asset value more than 12 calendar months old (15,556 oracle cells, 400/400 sampled confirmed as gap-bridges). Correct definition: AssetGrowth_t = (at_t - at_{t-12cal}) / at_{t-12cal}, NaN when the calendar t-12 observation does not exist, and NaN (not inf) when at_{t-12} == 0 — the zero guard matches the script's own L66-70, which we adopt; only the calendar-vs-positional lag semantics deviate.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Single input 'at' on availability-lagged time_avail_m; both lags reach backward. The script's gap-bridge cells use data that is too old, never future data.

rulings.justification: (1) ppent forward-fill (L49): a deliberate, commented imputation carrying the last reported net PP&E across missing months — a defensible research choice using only past data, and it accounts for 13,508 of 13,520 misses (proven at permno 33144 1967-04: ffill replication reproduces oracle -0.010254933 exactly). The engine must adopt it: wrap ppent as FFILL(ppent) inside both the current and LAG(...,12) copies of temp; wide-panel ffill is semantically equivalent because m_aCompustat is monthly-expanded (verified on the gap re-entry cell). Note the script otherwise uses proper calendar-merge lags (L65-69, L81-88), so there is no positional-lag issue here. (2) Retention of inf when average net operating assets are zero (12 residual cells, e.g. permno 11460 1991-04 where temp + temp_l12 = 0): a DEFECT — an infinite 'change in asset turnover' is economically meaningless and only exists because the script never scrubs non-finites on this path; the engine's non-finite masking is the correct definition (P4). Treatment: add FFILL to match the defensible part, keep the engine's inf->NaN behavior as a documented deviation, and exclude oracle infs in reconciliation. Fully tree-expressible; no demotion.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: ChAssetTurnover: We adopt the script's deliberate ppent forward-fill (ChAssetTurnover.py L49) inside temp = (rect+invt+aco+ffill(ppent)+intan)-(ap+lco+lo). We deviate in one place: when average net operating assets (temp + temp_l12)/2 equal zero, the script stores AssetTurnover = inf and can emit inf ChAssetTurnover (12 cells, e.g. permno 11460 1991-04); we define the ratio as NaN when its denominator is zero — an infinite turnover is not a value, it is an unguarded division. All lags are calendar-based in both implementations.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. All Compustat inputs on availability-lagged time_avail_m; ffill propagates only PAST ppent values forward; both 12-month lags are calendar merges on time_avail_m - 12 months. No forward-reaching operation exists in either implementation.

rulings.justification: Here the roles are reversed: the script is the calendar-correct implementation and both discrepancy classes are engine defects. (1) Lags: the script computes all six accrual-component lags via calendar-date-offset merges (create_calendar_lag, L63-78) — exactly the semantics our principles require; the engine's _op_chforecast_accrual_signal uses positional grouped.shift(12) (p1_factor_engine.py L2400-2409), which pulls stale across-gap values into tempAccruals and thereby perturbs the monthly qcut median pool for EVERY stock in the month (proven at permno 70578 1978-02: script pool n=3429 median 0.0158684 -> tempsort 2 vs engine pool n=3452 median 0.0160770 -> tempsort 1). The engine must switch to calendar merges. (2) Ticker mapping/universe: the script maps permno -> tickerIBES through SignalMasterTable (L47-51), which both applies the standard shrcd/exchcd universe and uses the SMT's point-in-time permno-ticker alignment — a deliberate, defensible design; the engine's IBESCRSPLinkingTable mapping on the unfiltered Compustat grid produces 62,805 extras (1,969/2,000 sampled outside SMT entirely) and must be replaced with the SMT-sourced mapping (or an SMT mask on the final panel). Both fixes live inside an already-bespoke long-form op (the monthly median split is irreducibly cross-sectional and cannot be a wide-grid tree anyway), so 'match_reference' here means correcting the op in place — demotion adds nothing since the op already reimplements the script's full pipeline. The script's zero/inf guards on tempAccruals (L94-95) are correct and already matched. No deviation retained.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. meanest is the IBES consensus published as of time_avail_m (statpers-dated) and meanest_l is the prior month's consensus (shift(1) backward in both implementations); accrual components are availability-lagged Compustat values at t and calendar t-12; the median split pools only month-t cross-sectional values. The engine's positional shift(12) defect fetches stale past data, not future data — a correctness (P2) issue, not a look-ahead (P3) violation.

rulings.justification: ChInv.py:38-40 applies positional groupby.shift(12) to deduplicated m_aCompustat rows. Where a permno's coverage has gaps, the 'annual' lag silently reaches 13-48+ calendar months back (proven: permno 29103 @ 1986-06 pairs with 1982-06 invt/at, 48 months stale, reproducing the oracle bit-exactly). Thomas & Zhang (2002) define a one-year inventory change, and OSAP's original Stata used tsset l12 calendar semantics; the repo even ships utils.stata_replication.stata_multi_lag with fill_gaps=True precisely to replicate calendar lags, and this script does not use it — evidence of a porting oversight, not a research choice. Under P1/P2 the engine's calendar LAG/DELTA (p1_factor_engine.py:704-714) is the provably correct definition; all 15,586 divergent cells are oracle artifacts (extra=0, all both-valued cells agree exactly). Do NOT add a positional-lag op to chase the oracle: that would encode multi-year changes as annual changes.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: ChInv: engine uses strict 12-calendar-month lags (DELTA(invt,12), LAG(at,12) on the monthly grid); reference ChInv.py:38-40 uses positional groupby.shift(12) on deduped m_aCompustat rows, so across coverage gaps its 'lag' uses data 13 to 48+ months old (e.g. permno 29103 @ 1986-06 uses 1982-06 balance-sheet data). The reference is wrong: Thomas & Zhang (2002) and OSAP's Stata original define a 12-calendar-month change; positional shift across gaps mislabels multi-year changes as annual. Correct definition: ChInv_t = (invt_t - invt_{t-12cal}) / ((at_t + at_{t-12cal})/2), NaN when no m_aCompustat observation exists exactly 12 calendar months prior. The 15,586 across-gap oracle cells are masked as oracle_artifact in reconciliation.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Inputs are m_aCompustat invt/at whose time_avail_m already embeds the datadate+6-month availability lag; both the script's positional shift(12) and the engine's calendar shift(12) reach strictly backward in time (rows sorted ascending, so a positional lag across a gap is older, never newer, data). No future information enters either side.

rulings.justification: Identical mechanism to ChInv: ChNNCOA.py:54 lags temp=((at-act-ivao)-(lt-dlc-dltt))/at with positional groupby.shift(12); across m_aCompustat coverage gaps the change spans more than 12 calendar months (proven: permno 18331 @ 1953-06 uses the 1951-06 row, 24 months back, matching the oracle exactly while calendar month 1952-06 is absent). Soliman (2008) DeltaNCO is a twelve-month change; the positional semantics are a porting artifact (the repo's stata_multi_lag/fill_gaps utility exists for exactly this and was not used). Engine calendar DELTA is correct; the 15,252 misses are oracle artifacts, extra=0, all overlapping cells agree exactly.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: ChNNCOA: engine uses a 12-calendar-month DELTA of NNCOA/at on the monthly grid; reference ChNNCOA.py:54 uses positional groupby.shift(12) on deduped m_aCompustat rows, so across coverage gaps the 'twelve-month change' spans 24+ months (e.g. permno 18331 @ 1953-06 differences against 1951-06). The reference is wrong: Soliman (2008) Table 7 DeltaNCO is an annual change and OSAP's Stata original used calendar l12. Correct definition: ChNNCOA_t = temp_t - temp_{t-12cal}, temp = ((at-act-ivao)-(lt-dlc-dltt))/at, NaN when the t-12-calendar-month observation is absent. The 15,252 across-gap oracle cells are masked as oracle_artifact.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. All inputs (at, act, ivao, lt, dlc, dltt) come from m_aCompustat with the built-in availability lag; script positional and engine calendar shifts both reach only backward. No look-ahead on either side.

rulings.justification: Same defect family: DelCOA.py:51-53 builds lag_at/lag_act/lag_che via positional groupby.shift(12); the 15,586-cell miss mask is bit-identical to ChInv's (same permnos, same gaps), and the positional replication at permno 29103 @ 1986-06 reproduces the oracle 0.3682718 using the 1982-06 row as the 'one-year' lag. Richardson et al. (2005) define the change in current operating assets over one fiscal year scaled by average assets; averaging at_t with an at from four years earlier is economically meaningless. Engine calendar DELTA/LAG is the correct definition (extra=0; all overlapping cells agree exactly).
rulings.deviation_register_entry: DelCOA: engine computes ((act-che)_t - (act-che)_{t-12cal}) / (0.5*(at_t + at_{t-12cal})) with strict calendar lags; reference DelCOA.py:51-53 uses positional groupby.shift(12), so across m_aCompustat coverage gaps the lagged act/che/at come from 13 to 48+ months earlier (miss mask bit-identical to ChInv's). The reference is wrong: Richardson et al. (2005) Table 8C is a one-year change scaled by one-year-average assets; OSAP's Stata original used calendar l12. Correct definition: NaN whenever no observation exists exactly 12 calendar months prior. The 15,586 across-gap oracle cells are masked as oracle_artifact.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. m_aCompustat inputs carry the availability lag; positional and calendar 12-period shifts are both strictly backward-looking. No future information used by either implementation.

rulings.justification: NOA.py:56 lags the scaling denominator at with positional groupby.shift(12). The proven extreme case (permno 81021 @ 2019-08 scaled by at from 2007-08 — eleven years stale — matching the oracle exactly) shows the quirk at its worst: Hirshleifer et al. (2004) scale net operating assets by beginning-of-year (one-year-lagged) total assets, and scaling 2019 NOA by 2007 assets is unambiguously unintended. The formula itself matches exactly (3,115,585 overlapping cells, max_abs=0, extra=0); only the 15,351 across-gap cells diverge. Engine calendar LAG is correct; keep it and mask the oracle artifacts.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: NOA: engine computes (OA-OL)/at_{t-12cal} with a strict calendar lag; reference NOA.py:56 uses positional groupby.shift(12), so across m_aCompustat coverage gaps the denominator is total assets from up to 12 years earlier (e.g. permno 81021 @ 2019-08 scaled by at from 2007-08). The reference is wrong: Hirshleifer et al. (2004) Table 4 scales by one-year-lagged total assets; OSAP's Stata original used calendar l12. Correct definition: NOA_t = ((at-che) - (at-dltt-mib-dc-ceq))_t / at_{t-12cal}, NaN when no observation exists exactly 12 calendar months prior. The 15,351 across-gap oracle cells are masked as oracle_artifact.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. All inputs from m_aCompustat with availability lag embedded in time_avail_m; both lag semantics reach only backward (the defect makes data staler, the opposite of look-ahead). No future information on either side.

rulings.justification: Two distinct quirks. (1) Universe conditioning (DebtIssuance.py:44,51,57-58): inner-merge to SignalMasterTable, null when shrcd>11 or BM=log(ceq/mve_permco) is NaN. This is DEFENSIBLE methodology — Spiess & Affleck-Graves (1999) construct their sample from common stocks matched on book-to-market, so requiring shrcd<=11 and a defined BM is a deliberate sample-construction choice; the engine must adopt it (it explains the 669k extras, all accounted for: not-in-SMT / shrcd>11 / BM NaN, 0 unexplained). This IS expressible on the wide grid: the engine already sources shrcd panels and applies shrcd<=11 masks (p1_factor_engine.py:1082-1094) and builds mve_permco/BM masks (lines 1387-1388, 1944-1947) plus SMT-universe masks (line 2738+), so demotion is not warranted. (2) Missing-dltis handling (line 54): ((dltis>0) & notna).astype(int) maps unreported dltis to 0 across 358k firm-months (sampled 1000/1000 misses are dltis=NaN with oracle 0). Although this mirrors the Stata original's (dltis>0 & dltis<.) coding, it is a DEFECT under P4: a missing cash-flow-statement item (concentrated in pre-funds-statement years) means issuance is UNOBSERVED, not zero; classifying unknown firm-months as non-issuers injects fabricated zeros into the long side of the portfolio. Engine keeps 1{dltis>0} with NaN where dltis is unreported, adds the universe/BM mask, and documents the deviation.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: DebtIssuance: engine adopts the reference's universe conditioning (SMT-matched permno-months, shrcd<=11, BM=log(ceq/mve_permco) defined) as correct methodology, but deviates on missing-data handling: reference DebtIssuance.py:54 (and the OSAP Stata original) codes DebtIssuance=0 when dltis is missing, silently classifying ~358k firm-months with unreported debt issuance (largely pre-funds-statement-era Compustat) as non-issuers.
