The reference is wrong under NaN discipline: an unreported cash-flow item is unobserved, not zero. Correct definition: DebtIssuance = 1 if dltis>0, 0 if dltis reported and <=0, NaN if dltis unreported; restricted to SMT common stocks (shrcd<=11) with defined log book-to-market. Oracle cells whose only support is the NaN-to-0 fill are masked as oracle_artifact in reconciliation.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. dltis and ceq come from m_aCompustat (time_avail_m = datadate + availability lag); shrcd and mve_permco come from SignalMasterTable at the signal month t itself (end-of-month-t CRSP data, available before the t+1 return the signal predicts). BM mixes lagged book equity with current market equity, which is the standard point-in-time construction, not look-ahead. Neither implementation uses future information.

rulings.justification: The script's quirks are deliberate research choices from Zhang (2006), and the divergence here is the ENGINE's error, not the script's. (a) Filtering |prc|>=5-or-NaN AND age>=12 BEFORE the monthly pd.qcut (FirmAgeMom.py:43-44,60-62) is correct: Zhang 2006 Section II excludes sub-$5 stocks from the sample, so age quintiles must be formed on the surviving universe. The engine's _op_firm_age_momentum (p1_factor_engine.py:966-971) buckets ALL aged firms first and masks after — a wrong-universe ranking (2000-06: q1 cutoff age<=41 on n=4,669 filtered vs age<=28 on n=8,282 unfiltered), which is why overlap is only 189,950 cells. (b) age = per-permno SMT row count is the standard 'months since listing' proxy. (c) ret.fillna(0) applied to surviving SMT rows before compounding is the OSAP momentum convention (deliberate, applied only where the security exists in SMT — not a grid-wide zero-fill, so tolerable under P4). (d) Lags via stata_multi_lag with fill_gaps=True are proper calendar lags. Demotion criteria are met: the logic is sound AND the wide-grid engine genuinely cannot express it — it needs SMT-row-domain age counting, a row filter that runs before both the cross-sectional qcut (with duplicates='drop' tie semantics under massive age ties) and the lag construction (filtered-out months must yield NULL lags), which are row-domain filter-then-rank composites the calendar-grid DSL has no ops for. Fixing _op_firm_age_momentum to filter-before-bucket would still not reproduce SMT row-count age or qcut tie handling.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean in both. Script: signal at month t uses age through t (past row count), prc at t, and returns t-5..t-1 (stata_multi_lag lags 1-5, current-month return excluded); the monthly qcut uses only month-t cross-sectional ages; everything is known at end of month t, before the t+1 return it predicts. Engine version is likewise backward-looking (compound_return over lags 1-5, age from past presence). No future information in either implementation.

rulings.justification: The formula (GrLTNOA.py L94-129) is faithfully replicated by the engine (3,139,905 both-valued cells, max_abs=0), so the only divergence is the lag mechanism. The script's positional groupby.shift(12) (L83-86) is a DEFECT under P1/P2: it silently computes an 'annual' growth in net operating assets against a lag base that can be decades old when m_aCompustat coverage has gaps (permno 11275: t=2020-10 base=1990-12, 30 years; permno 68276: t=2015-08 base=1982-08). Fairfield-Whisenant-Yohn 2003 defines annual growth over one fiscal year; a 30-year delta scaled as if it were one year of growth is economically meaningless, and the script produces it silently with no gap check. All 15,333 miss cells are this pattern (12/12 sampled gap-lag, has_calendar_t12=False in every sample); extra=0. The engine's calendar lag returning NaN when no observation exists at t-12 is the correct definition and also satisfies P4 (no value where none is genuinely defined). POSITIONAL_LAG bit-replication is rejected: reproducing a defect for parity contradicts P2.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: GrLTNOA — engine deviates from OSAP GrLTNOA.py L83-86. Reference computes 12-month lags of the 10 balance-sheet inputs via positional groupby.shift(12) over m_aCompustat rows; across coverage gaps the lag base month can be years-to-decades before t-12 (observed up to 30 years), so the reference values an 'annual growth in LTNOA' against an arbitrarily stale base. Correct definition: all lagged inputs are taken at calendar month t-12 exactly; if the firm has no m_aCompustat observation at t-12, GrLTNOA is NaN at t. Impact: 15,333 oracle-only cells are dropped as artifacts; zero extras; all shared cells match to 0 abs error.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. All inputs (rect, invt, ppent, aco, intan, ao, ap, lco, lo, at, dp) come from m_aCompustat, whose time_avail_m already embeds the accounting availability lag from datadate; both implementations read values at t or t-12 only. The script's positional shift always reaches >= 12 months backward (never forward), so its defect is staleness, not look-ahead. Engine calendar lag is strictly backward. Neither implementation uses future information.

rulings.justification: Two independent quirks. (1) The zero-denominator guard (InvestPPEInv.py L82-86: l12_at==0 -> NaN) is DEFENSIBLE METHODOLOGY — investment scaled by zero lagged assets is undefined, and NaN is the correct P4 semantics. The engine's current behavior (_op_div at p1_factor_engine.py:688 emits inf, which survives as a valued cell — all 30 extras, e.g. permno 82716 2000-06..2001-05) is an ENGINE defect and must be fixed to match the script: DIV(ADD(delta(ppegt,12),delta(invt,12)), ZERO_TO_NULL(LAG(at,12))). (2) The positional shift(12) (L68-70) is a DEFECT identical to GrLTNOA: 'one-year change in PPE plus inventory scaled by lagged assets' (Lyandres-Sun-Zhang 2008) computed against a base up to 22 years old (permno 12928: t=2023-12 base=2001-12) is not the stated economics. All 14,319 misses are gap-lag artifacts (12/12 sampled); engine calendar-lag NaN is correct. Both-valued cells agree exactly, confirming the formula itself. Net treatment: match the reference's zero-guard (engine fix), deviate documented on the lag mechanism.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: InvestPPEInv — engine deviates from OSAP InvestPPEInv.py L68-70. Reference computes l12_ppegt/l12_invt/l12_at via positional groupby.shift(12); across m_aCompustat gaps the 'one-year' change spans up to 22+ years. Correct definition: delta(ppegt,12), delta(invt,12) and lag(at,12) taken at calendar t-12 exactly; NaN when no t-12 observation exists. The reference's l12_at==0 -> NaN guard (L82-86) is adopted as correct (engine tree amended with ZERO_TO_NULL on the denominator, eliminating 30 spurious inf cells). Impact: 14,319 oracle-only gap-lag cells dropped as artifacts; shared cells match exactly.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. ppegt, invt, at all from m_aCompustat with availability-lagged time_avail_m; both implementations reference t and t-12 only. Positional shift reaches only backward (>=12 months); engine calendar lag exactly t-12. The engine's inf cells use at(t-12)=0 — wrong semantics but still historical data. Neither uses future information.

rulings.justification: Formula parity is proven (tree zero_to_null(div(ob,(at+lag(at,12))/2)) vs OrderBacklog.py L36-39; 626,994 both-valued, max_abs=0; the ob==0 -> NaN rule at L39 is equivalent to the engine's zero_to_null on the ratio since the ratio is 0 iff ob=0). The sole divergence is the positional shift(12) at L33 — a DEFECT: the denominator is meant to be average total assets over the current and prior year (Rajgopal-Shevlin-Venkatachalam 2003), but across gaps the script averages at(t) with at from up to 8+ years earlier (permno 86319: t=2007-07 base=1999-07; permno 31608: t=1990-03 base=1984-03), producing a scale that is neither current nor one-year-lagged assets. All 3,033 misses are this pattern (12/12 sampled, has_calendar_t12=False); extra=0. Engine calendar-lag NaN is correct and P4-consistent. POSITIONAL_LAG replication rejected under P2.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: OrderBacklog — engine deviates from OSAP OrderBacklog.py L33. Reference lags at via positional groupby.shift(12), so across m_aCompustat gaps the 'average total assets' denominator mixes at(t) with at from a month up to 8+ years before t-12. Correct definition: OrderBacklog = ob / (0.5*(at(t) + at(t-12 calendar))), NaN when ob=0 or no observation exists at calendar t-12. Impact: 3,033 oracle-only gap-lag cells dropped as artifacts; zero extras; all shared cells match to 0 abs error.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. ob and at from m_aCompustat (availability-lagged time_avail_m); references are t and t-12 only in both implementations; positional shift reaches only backward. Neither uses future information.

rulings.justification: The 4,000 extras are ENGINE omissions of DEFENSIBLE script methodology that must be matched: (a) dropping SIC 6000-6999 financials and requiring ceq>0 OR ceq missing (L78-80) are standard, deliberate Boudoukh-et-al-2007 universe choices; (b) the SignalMasterTable inner join (L38) is a deliberate universe filter; (c) the >=24-observation seasoning gate (L86-87) is a stated stability choice and is point-in-time (cumcount counts only past+current rows); (d) requiring the t-6 mve_permco base to be an SMT-x-Compustat row (self-merge L47-56) follows from the universe definition. All are expressible on the wide grid: NONFINANCIAL_ONLY + ceq mask + SMT mask + a cumulative post-filter-valid-count >= 24 mask (cumsum of the eligibility mask per permno column), so demotion is NOT justified under the new rule. The gate's exact count domain (after zero/SIC/ceq drops, before NaN drop) is script-shaped but reproducible with the mask-cumsum construction. The one DEFECT is the 1e-19 sentinel (L62-68): when dvc+prstkc-sstk nets to exactly 0 with nonzero components (permno 50606 1987-12: prstkc=sstk=18.495), the script overwrites the true value 0 with the arbitrary constant 1e-19 to survive its own !=0 filter — a Stata-replication hack that stores a fabricated number. All 828 misses are this sentinel. Correct definition: NPY=0 is genuinely defined there (P4: a value exists), so the engine keeps the cell valued at 0.0; cells where all three components are 0 (or missing) remain excluded per the script's intent.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: NetPayoutYield — engine matches all reference filters (non-financial SIC, ceq>0-or-missing, SignalMasterTable universe, SMT-based t-6 mve_permco lag, >=24 prior eligible observations with the count taken over post-zero/SIC/ceq-filter rows) but deviates from OSAP NetPayoutYield.py L62-68: where (dvc+prstkc-sstk)/mve_l6 nets to exactly 0 with at least one nonzero component, the reference stores the sentinel 1e-19; the engine stores the true value 0.0. Reason: 1e-19 is a fabricated constant used only to defeat the script's own zero-drop filter; the economically defined value is 0. Impact: 828 cells valued 0.0 in engine vs 1e-19 in oracle; observations where dvc=prstkc=sstk=0 remain excluded in both.

Neither implementation uses future information.

rulings.justification: The script's logic is sound throughout: keeping only the smallest size tercile (RDcap.py L71-76) implements Li 2011 Table 7 (effect exists only in small firms) — a deliberate research choice; zero-filling missing xrd within each permno's Compustat span (fill_date_gaps L51 + fillna(0) L54) reflects the standard assumption that unreported R&D is zero for a firm that is filing; the 48-month weighted R&D capital and the pre-1980 exclusion are per the reference paper. The empty engine panel is 100% an ENGINE defect: _op_size_filtered's signature default min_tercile=2 combined with the spec passing only {max_tercile: 1} yields the provably empty mask (rank_pct > 1/3) & (rank_pct <= 1/3). Fix: pass {min_tercile: null, max_tercile: 1} (and harden the op so an explicit max_* suppresses the min_tercile default — this default is a footgun that also hit std_turn). Two secondary engine corrections needed for a faithful match, both P4 issues on the engine side: (1) restrict the xrd fillna(0) to each firm's m_aCompustat first-to-last-observation span — the current grid-wide fillna manufactures RDcap values in months where the firm has no accounting existence; (2) lags landing before the span must stay NaN so each firm's first 48 months are NaN as in the script. Residual caveat to verify at reconciliation: pd.qcut tercile breakpoints (interpolated quantiles, computed only over firms with non-null mve_c) vs the engine's rank_pct <= 1/3 can disagree for boundary firms; if material, implement qcut-equivalent per-month breakpoints rather than accepting the diff.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. xrd lags reference t-12..t-48 (backward only, calendar-based via stata_multi_lag in the script and calendar lag in the engine); at is at t; the size tercile is computed cross-sectionally within month t on SMT mve_c, which is known at t. Neither implementation uses future information.

rulings.justification: Three components. (1) DEFENSIBLE: restricting to size quintiles 1-3 on mve_c = shrout*|prc| from monthlyCRSP (std_turn.py L54-67) is the deliberate Chordia-Subrahmanyam-Anshuman 2001 Table 5B choice (tiny spread in large firms); the engine must match it — including computing size from monthlyCRSP shrout*|prc|, not mve_permco, and using qcut-equivalent per-month quintile breakpoints, since the 208,886 extras are engine cells in script-quintile 4 admitted by the rank_pct<=3/5 boundary (e.g. permno 10644, rank 0.589, qcut q=4). qcut breakpoints are expressible on the wide grid (per-month interpolated quantiles of the size panel), so this is matchable, not demote-worthy. (2) ENGINE DEFECT: the size_filtered spec passed only {max_quintile: 3}, so the min_tercile=2 signature default silently intersected in a bottom-tercile exclusion (keeping only rank in (1/3, 3/5]) — the dominant cause of the 1,412,309 misses; fix with min_tercile: null (same footgun as RDcap; the op should reject implicit defaults when only max_* is supplied). (3) SCRIPT DEFECT: rolling_std over trailing 36 ROWS (L47-52, polars over permno with no gap fill) means that for a permno with listing gaps, the '36-month' turnover volatility actually spans an arbitrarily longer calendar window mixing observations across delistings/re-listings — the same positional-across-gap staleness defect as the shift(12) cases, contradicting the stated 'past 36 months' definition. Correct definition: std over calendar months t-35..t with >=24 valid turnover observations; the engine's calendar window implements this and the residual diffs on gapped permnos are documented artifacts, not errors. Demotion is rejected: it would reproduce defect (3) and the script's remaining logic is fully expressible.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: std_turn — engine deviates from OSAP std_turn.py L47-52. Reference computes rolling_std of turnover (vol/shrout) over the trailing 36 ROWS per permno with min 24 samples; for permnos with listing gaps this window spans more than 36 calendar months, mixing pre- and post-gap turnover regimes while labeling the result 'past 36 months volatility'. Correct definition: standard deviation of monthly turnover over calendar months t-35..t, requiring >=24 non-null months, NaN otherwise. The reference's size screen is adopted as correct and matched exactly: size = shrout*|prc| from monthlyCRSP, per-month pd.qcut-equivalent quintile breakpoints, values kept for quintiles 1-3, null when quintile>=4 or size is missing (spec fix: min_tercile null so no implicit bottom-tercile exclusion). Impact: cells for gap-spanning windows differ from oracle by construction; boundary-quintile extras eliminated by qcut-equivalent breakpoints.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. Turnover uses vol/shrout at months <= t; the rolling window is strictly trailing in both implementations (rows in the script, calendar months in the engine — both backward-only); the size quintile is computed cross-sectionally within month t from prices/shares known at t. Neither implementation uses future information.

rulings.justification: The intended methodology (Richardson et al. 2005: balance-sheet accruals pre-1990, cash-flow method after, with missing supplementary items ivao/ivst/dltt/dlc/pstk/sstk/prstkc/dv treated as zero) is defensible, and the script itself declares that intent by creating zero-filled temps at TotalAccruals.py L53-55. But the execution contains three defects under P1/P4: (1) the late branch at L88-92 uses raw df['sstk']-df['prstkc']-df['dv'] instead of the temps it just created — dead-code temps are the signature of a translation bug, and the effect is 22,346 post-1989 firm-months silently dropped solely because a supplementary item is missing (economically unintended firm attrition; the 3,193/3,193 sampled extras all have raw sstk/prstkc/dv missing while the formula is otherwise computable). (2) Positional groupby.shift(12) at L67-70 reaches rows more than 12 calendar months back across m_aCompustat gaps (permno 18331 t=1953-06 lags to 1951-06), violating the stated 12-month window — the original Stata l12. operator is calendar-based, so the pyCode deviates from its own source. (3) at_lag12==0 produces inf at L95 that survives dropna (108 oracle inf cells) — inf is not a defined signal value; scaling by zero assets is undefined and must be NaN under P4. The engine's existing behavior (zero-filled temps in the late branch at p1_factor_engine.py L2289, calendar shift(12), np.isfinite mask at L2293) is correct on all three points. Do NOT apply the prior proposed fix that would switch the engine to raw sstk/prstkc/dv to match the script; the remaining ~14.8k calendar-vs-positional misses and 108 inf cells are oracle artifacts to be accepted, not reproduced.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: TotalAccruals — deviates from OSAP pyCode TotalAccruals.py in three ways. (1) Late (post-1989) branch: engine uses zero-filled sstk/prstkc/dv (late = ni - (oancf+ivncf+fincf) + (sstk0 - prstkc0 - dv0)); the script creates these zero-filled temps at L53-55 but then accidentally uses the raw columns at L88-92, so any missing supplementary item NaNs the whole signal and drops the firm-month. The zero-fill is the documented Richardson et al. (2005) treatment and matches the script's own declared intent; the raw-variable use is a pyCode translation bug (~22.3k firm-months silently lost). (2) 12-month lag: engine uses calendar t-12 on the monthly wide grid; the script's positional groupby.shift(12) reaches arbitrarily stale rows across m_aCompustat coverage gaps (observed lags to 30+ months), violating the 12-month definition; the original Stata l12. is calendar. Engine emits NaN when no calendar t-12 row exists (~14.9k oracle cells not reproduced, by design). (3) at_lag12==0: engine returns NaN (undefined scaling); the script emits inf which survives its dropna (108 oracle cells). Correct definition: TotalAccruals_t = [dWC + dNC + dFI]/at_{t-12} for year<=1989 and [ni - (oancf+ivncf+fincf) + (sstk0-prstkc0-dv0)]/at_{t-12} for year>1989, all lags calendar 12-month, result NaN when at_{t-12} is missing or zero.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. All inputs are m_aCompustat items at time_avail_m (annual accounting data already carrying the OSAP availability lag from datadate); the 12-month lags reach strictly older data in both implementations. The script's positional shift defect reaches BACKWARD beyond 12 months (stale data), never forward — a staleness defect, not look-ahead. No price, IBES, or future-dated input enters either implementation.

rulings.justification: Both script behaviors flagged as quirks are deliberate, sound research choices, and the discrepancy is an engine gap, not a script defect. (1) The accrual-based fallback (cfp.py L94-129): when oancf is missing — i.e., the entire pre-SFAS-95 era before ~1988 — the script computes operating cash flow as ib minus balance-sheet accruals, accrual_level = (d12.act - d12.che) - (d12.lct - d12.dlc - d12.txp - dp), with oancf/mve overriding whenever oancf is reported. This is exactly the Desai, Rajgopal, Venkatachalam (2004) construction and is what gives the factor its 1960s-1980s history; the engine's bare DIV(oancf, mve_permco) tree silently truncates 689,150 firm-months of the sample. Critically, the script's 12-month lags here are CALENDAR-based self-merges on time_avail_m minus 12 months (L98-101), so it does not even have the positional-shift defect seen elsewhere. (2) The inner merge with SignalMasterTable (L66-84) restricts output to the OSAP common-stock universe (shrcd 10/11/12, exchcd 1/2/3) — a standard, deliberate universe filter; the engine's 241,141 extras (sampled shrcd 71/31/18) are ADRs, certificates, and units outside the intended universe. (3) mve_permco==0 -> NaN (L117-121) is correct P4 discipline. Fix the engine: cfp = COALESCE(DIV(oancf, mve0), DIV(ib - accrual_level, mve0)) with calendar 12-month lags and zero_to_null on mve_permco, output masked to SMT membership. The wide grid can express all of this, so demotion is not warranted.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. Script: accounting items (act, che, lct, dlc, txp, dp, ib, oancf) come from m_aCompustat at time_avail_m with the standard OSAP availability lag; the accrual lags are calendar t-12 self-merges reaching strictly older rows; mve_permco comes from SignalMasterTable at the signal month (point-in-time market equity). Engine: same inputs; adding the accrual branch with calendar LAG(.,12) introduces only older data. Neither implementation uses any information dated after the signal month.

rulings.justification: The single quirk is the positional groupby('permno').shift(12) at SurpriseRD.py L33-34. The factor's definition (Eberhart, Maxwell, Siddique 2004) compares current R&D to R&D twelve months prior; the original Stata code used calendar l12. operators. Across m_aCompustat coverage gaps the positional shift silently compares xrd_t against xrd from 21-28 months earlier (8/8 sampled miss cells confirm no calendar t-12 row exists: e.g. permno 36062 t=1971-12 lags to 1970-03), so the 'surprise' is measured against a stale base — a lag reaching further back than the stated window, which is the definition of a DEFECT under the task rubric, not a research choice. The engine (_op_surprise_rd_indicator, p1_factor_engine.py L1171-1185) uses calendar lag on the monthly grid and correctly emits NaN when no t-12 observation exists. Reconciliation shows cells_beyond_tol=0 and extra=0: everywhere both sides emit a value they agree exactly, and the 6,728 misses (0.44% of oracle cells) are all stale-lag oracle emissions. Accept the engine behavior and register the deviation. Demotion to script is unjustified: the script logic at the divergence point is unsound, and the engine expresses the sound version natively.
rulings.deviation_register_entry: SurpriseRD — deviates from OSAP pyCode SurpriseRD.py on the 12-month lag semantics. The script uses positional groupby(permno).shift(12) (L33-34), which across m_aCompustat coverage gaps compares current xrd against an observation more than 12 calendar months old (stale base for the surprise conditions xrd/xrd_lag12 > 1.05 and (xrd/at)/(xrd_lag12/at_lag12) > 1.05), emitting ~6.7k firm-months where no true t-12 observation exists. The original Stata implementation used calendar l12. lags. The engine uses calendar t-12 lags on the monthly wide grid and emits NaN when the permno has no m_aCompustat row at t-12 (condition6 fails). Correct definition: SurpriseRD_t = 1 if xrd_t/revt_t>0, xrd_t/at_t>0, xrd_t/xrd_{t-12}>1.05, and (xrd_t/at_t)/(xrd_{t-12}/at_{t-12})>1.05, with both xrd_t and xrd_{t-12} observed at calendar t-12; 0 if both observed but conditions fail; NaN otherwise. Zero value disagreements exist where both implementations emit a value.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. Inputs are xrd, revt, at from m_aCompustat at time_avail_m (availability-lagged annual data) and their 12-month lags. The script's positional shift reaches OLDER rows than calendar t-12 (staleness, backward-looking); the engine's calendar lag reaches exactly t-12. Neither implementation touches any observation dated after the signal month.

rulings.justification: VolSD.py is a clean implementation of Chordia, Subrahmanyam, Anshuman (2001): trailing 36-month rolling standard deviation of monthly volume with min_samples=24, per permno (L40-47). Nothing in the script is a quirk — the window, the minimum-observation threshold, and the per-permno grouping are all standard, deliberate choices. The 14,283 beyond-tolerance cells are proven to be a stale ORACLE, not a script or engine defect: re-executing the script's exact computation on current monthlyCRSP matches the engine everywhere to float32 precision (maxdiff 2.4e-4) while disagreeing with the oracle at 87,881 cells, the mismatches sit in contiguous <=46-month runs (the 36-month contamination footprint of revised raw vol observations), and the oracle contains values impossible under current data (a value at 21 available rows against min_samples=24; 310/415 mismatch permnos with oracle series starting earlier than current data permits). Under P2 the engine is already independently proven correct against the reference LOGIC; what fails is the reference DATA vintage. Therefore: regenerate the VolSD oracle from the current monthlyCRSP.parquet by running VolSD.py as-is, then re-reconcile. No engine change to the value computation. The only engine-side item is the separately identified fill-domain masking (P4): output must exist only at permno-months present in monthlyCRSP, never propagated onto grid months where the stock has no volume observation.
rulings.lookahead_check: Clean. The 36-month rolling window is strictly trailing (observations t-35..t of monthly volume, all realized by the end of the signal month) in both the script's rolling_std(36, min_samples=24).over(permno) and the engine's native rolling implementation. min_samples gates on past observation count only. Neither implementation uses volume, prices, or membership information from after the signal month. The oracle-vs-current differences stem from retroactive CRSP data revisions between vintages, which is a data-vintage issue, not look-ahead in either implementation.
